review: 115.7a-1: base said Grizzly Bears was 'undamaged' after a destroy effect it never faced; reworded to 'stays on the battlefield'.
115.7f-1: 'declines' variant retargets nothing, so 115.7f does not apply to it; polarity does_not_fire changed to other (a division cannot be changed, so no does_not_fire exists).

115.8-1: the Izzet Charm variant retargeted to a player, which no mode of Izzet Charm can target, so it never tested that the mode is kept; rebuilt with Rakdos Charm (destroy target artifact) where the rejected new target, player A, fits the unchosen graveyard-exile mode.

scenarios.title: Only permanents are legal targets unless the spell names another zone
decisions: A's playable candidates are evaluated with Giant Growth as the candidate spell; no spell is cast.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Giant Growth (target creature) has exactly one legal target, Grizzly Bears on the battlefield; Runeclaw Bear in A's graveyard is not offered; can_play is true.

variants.label: no-permanent
variants.delta: Grizzly Bears is not on the battlefield, so the only creature is Runeclaw Bear in the graveyard.
variants.expected: Giant Growth has no legal target (the graveyard card is not a permanent); has_legal_target is false and can_play is false.

variants.label: graveyard-spell
variants.delta: The candidate spell is Raise Dead (target creature card in your graveyard) instead of Giant Growth.
variants.expected: Raise Dead's legal target list is exactly Runeclaw Bear in the graveyard; Grizzly Bears on the battlefield is not offered; can_play is true.

scenarios.title: One instance of the word target cannot choose the same object twice
decisions: A considers casting Arc Lightning (3 damage divided among one, two or three targets) tapping three Mountains, with the division 2 and 1 between two chosen targets.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: With the target list [Grizzly Bears, Grizzly Bears] the second pick is not legal: one instance of the word target cannot choose the same creature twice, so Arc Lightning cannot be cast with that list.

variants.label: distinct
variants.delta: The two targets are Grizzly Bears (2 damage) and Llanowar Elves (1 damage).
variants.expected: The target list [Grizzly Bears, Llanowar Elves] is legal and Arc Lightning can be cast with it.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge builds divided-damage targets one at a time, so the verdict shows up as the second pick not being offered.

scenarios.title: Separate instances of the word target may choose the same object
decisions: A casts Agony Warp, tapping Island and Swamp, choosing Grizzly Bears as the target of both the -3/-0 and the -0/-3 instances.
Both players pass; Agony Warp resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a legal target of both instances, gets -3/-0 and -0/-3 until end of turn (-1/-1), and moves to B's graveyard in the state-based check; Llanowar Elves is untouched.

variants.label: different
variants.delta: The -0/-3 instance targets Llanowar Elves instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears becomes -1/2 until end of turn and stays on the battlefield; Llanowar Elves becomes 1/-2 and moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: Any target offers only creatures, players, planeswalkers and battles
decisions: A considers casting Lightning Bolt, tapping Mountain, with one chosen target; the chosen target is Sol Ring.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Sol Ring (a noncreature artifact) is not a legal target of Lightning Bolt and is not in its legal target list.

variants.label: creature
variants.delta: The chosen target is Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a legal target of Lightning Bolt.

variants.label: player
variants.delta: The chosen target is player B.
variants.expected: Player B is a legal target of Lightning Bolt.

variants.label: planeswalker
variants.delta: The chosen target is Jace Beleren.
variants.expected: Jace Beleren is a legal target of Lightning Bolt.

scenarios.title: A spell on the stack is not a legal target for itself
decisions: B considers casting Counterspell, tapping two Islands, with priority and the stack as described.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The stack is empty, so Counterspell has no legal target (it is not a target for itself); has_legal_target is false and can_play is false.

variants.label: other-spell
variants.delta: Lightning Bolt controlled by A, targeting Grizzly Bears, is on the stack.
variants.expected: Counterspell's legal target list is exactly Lightning Bolt; Counterspell itself is not offered; can_play is true.

scenarios.forge_notes: In the second variant the stack object is placed on the stack in setup as {"card": "Lightning Bolt", "controller": "A", "targets": ["Grizzly Bears"]}.

scenarios.title: A target change succeeds only when another legal target exists
decisions: A casts Doom Blade, tapping both Swamps, targeting Grizzly Bears. A passes priority.
B casts Swerve, tapping Island and Mountain, targeting Doom Blade, and passes; A passes.
Swerve resolves: B changes Doom Blade's target to another legal target if one exists.
Both players pass; Doom Blade resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Doom Blade's target is changed to Hill Giant; Hill Giant moves to A's graveyard and Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: no-other-target
variants.delta: A's other creature is Typhoid Rats (black) instead of Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Typhoid Rats is not a legal target of Doom Blade, so no other legal target exists and the original target is unchanged; Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard and Typhoid Rats stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.forge_notes: A's own creature is a legal retarget for A's Doom Blade; B (the Swerve controller) chooses the new target.

scenarios.title: Changing a target alters only one target, and only to a legal one
decisions: A casts Arc Trail, tapping both Mountains: 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, 1 damage to Llanowar Elves. A passes priority.
B activates Spellskite paying {U/P} with Island, targeting Arc Trail, changing the first target (Grizzly Bears) to Spellskite, and passes; A passes.
Spellskite's ability resolves; both players pass; Arc Trail resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Only the first target changes: Spellskite is dealt 2 damage and survives (0/4), Llanowar Elves is dealt 1 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Grizzly Bears is undamaged.

variants.label: already-target
variants.delta: Arc Trail's second target is Spellskite instead of Llanowar Elves.
variants.expected: Changing the first target to Spellskite would leave both targets as Spellskite, which is illegal, so no target changes: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Spellskite is dealt 1 damage and survives, Llanowar Elves is undamaged.

variants.label: second-target
variants.delta: B changes the second target (Llanowar Elves) to Spellskite instead of the first.
variants.expected: Only the second target changes: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Spellskite is dealt 1 damage and survives, Llanowar Elves is undamaged.

scenarios.forge_notes: In the already-target variant Llanowar Elves stays on B's battlefield as in the base setup.

scenarios.title: Changing any targets lets any number of targets change
decisions: A casts Toils of Night and Day, tapping three Islands: first target Grizzly Bears, second target Llanowar Elves, choosing to tap each. A passes priority.
B casts Sideswipe, tapping both Mountains, targeting Toils of Night and Day, and passes; A passes.
Sideswipe resolves: B changes the first target (Grizzly Bears) to Hill Giant and leaves the second target.
Both players pass; Toils of Night and Day resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: One of two targets changed: Hill Giant becomes tapped, Llanowar Elves becomes tapped, Grizzly Bears stays untapped.

variants.label: both
variants.delta: B changes the first target to Hill Giant and the second target to Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Both targets changed: Hill Giant becomes tapped, Grizzly Bears becomes tapped, Llanowar Elves stays untapped.

variants.label: illegal-change
variants.delta: B tries to change the first target to Llanowar Elves and leaves the second target Llanowar Elves.
variants.expected: The final target set (Llanowar Elves twice) is illegal for Toils of Night and Day's 'another target', so no target changes: Grizzly Bears and Llanowar Elves become tapped, Hill Giant stays untapped.

scenarios.forge_notes: Toils of Night and Day is an Arcane instant, the only kind of spell Sideswipe can target.

scenarios.title: Choosing new targets may leave an illegal target unchanged
decisions: A casts Arc Trail, tapping both Mountains: 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, 1 damage to Llanowar Elves. A passes priority.
B casts Vines of Vastwood (unkicked) with Forest targeting Grizzly Bears, and passes; A passes; Vines of Vastwood resolves, so A's spells can no longer target Grizzly Bears.
A passes priority; B casts Redirect, tapping both Islands, targeting Arc Trail, and passes; A passes.
Redirect resolves: B leaves the first target (Grizzly Bears, now illegal) unchanged and changes the second target (Llanowar Elves) to player A.
Both players pass; Arc Trail resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Redirect succeeds with the illegal first target kept: Grizzly Bears is not dealt damage (illegal target), player A is dealt 1 damage (life 19), Llanowar Elves is undamaged; Arc Trail partially fizzles.

variants.label: illegal-new-target
variants.delta: B tries to change the second target to Sol Ring instead of player A.
variants.expected: Sol Ring is not a legal target for 'any other target', so the change is not made and the targets stay Grizzly Bears and Llanowar Elves: Grizzly Bears is not dealt damage (illegal), Llanowar Elves is dealt 1 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: Targets may be swapped because only the final target set is checked
decisions: A casts Arc Trail, tapping both Mountains: 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, 1 damage to Llanowar Elves. A passes priority.
B casts Redirect, tapping both Islands, targeting Arc Trail, and passes; A passes.
Redirect resolves: B chooses Llanowar Elves as the new first target and Grizzly Bears as the new second target.
Both players pass; Arc Trail resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The swap is allowed: Llanowar Elves is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Grizzly Bears is dealt 1 damage and stays with 1 damage marked.

variants.label: same-twice
variants.delta: B chooses Llanowar Elves as the new first target and leaves the second target Llanowar Elves.
variants.expected: The final set (Llanowar Elves twice) is illegal for 'any other target', so no target changes: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Llanowar Elves is dealt 1 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: Retargeting a divided effect keeps its original division
decisions: A casts Arc Lightning, tapping three Mountains: 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, 1 damage to Llanowar Elves. A passes priority.
B casts Redirect, tapping both Islands, targeting Arc Lightning, and passes; A passes.
Redirect resolves: B changes the first target (Grizzly Bears) to player A.
Both players pass; Arc Lightning resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The 2-damage share moves with the first target: player A is dealt 2 damage (life 18), Llanowar Elves is dealt 1 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Grizzly Bears is undamaged.

variants.label: second-slot
variants.delta: B changes the second target (Llanowar Elves) to player A instead.
variants.expected: The 1-damage share moves with the second target: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, player A is dealt 1 damage (life 19), Llanowar Elves is undamaged.

variants.label: declines
variants.delta: B chooses to leave both targets unchanged.
variants.expected: Nothing is retargeted: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard, Llanowar Elves is dealt 1 damage and moves to B's graveyard, player A's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: Retargeting a modal spell cannot switch it to another mode's target
decisions: A casts Rakdos Charm, tapping Swamp and Mountain, choosing the mode 'Destroy target artifact' and targeting Sol Ring. A passes priority.
B casts Redirect, tapping both Islands, targeting Rakdos Charm, and passes; A passes.
Redirect resolves: B chooses Mind Stone as the new target.
Both players pass; Rakdos Charm resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The mode is unchanged and only the target changes: Mind Stone moves to A's graveyard, Sol Ring stays on the battlefield, Grizzly Bears stays in A's graveyard.

variants.label: other-mode-target
variants.delta: B tries to choose player A as the new target instead of Mind Stone.
variants.expected: Player A is a legal target only of the unchosen graveyard-exile mode, so the target is not changed: Sol Ring moves to B's graveyard, Mind Stone stays on the battlefield, Grizzly Bears stays in A's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: Rakdos Charm's chosen Smash mode targets Artifact; its Exile mode targets Player.

scenarios.title: A spell with a single target counts the targets chosen, repeats included
decisions: A casts Shock, tapping Mountain, targeting Grizzly Bears.
Spinerock Tyrant's trigger goes on the stack; A copies Shock and chooses Llanowar Elves as the copy's target; both spells gain wither.
Both players pass; the copy resolves, then Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Shock has a single target, so Spinerock Tyrant's trigger fires and creates a copy: Llanowar Elves and Grizzly Bears each get two -1/-1 counters (wither) and move to B's graveyard.

variants.label: two-targets-same-creature
variants.delta: A casts Agony Warp (tapping Island and Swamp) choosing Grizzly Bears as the target of both instances instead of casting Shock.
variants.expected: The spell has two targets even though both are the same creature, so Spinerock Tyrant's trigger does not fire; Grizzly Bears gets -3/-0 and -0/-3 and moves to B's graveyard, Llanowar Elves is untouched.

variants.label: two-different-targets
variants.delta: A casts Agony Warp choosing Grizzly Bears for -3/-0 and Llanowar Elves for -0/-3 instead of casting Shock.
variants.expected: The spell has two targets, so the trigger does not fire; Grizzly Bears becomes -1/2 and stays, Llanowar Elves moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: The trigger is optional ('you may copy it'); the scenario assumes A takes it. Spinerock Tyrant tests the number of chosen targets through the .singleTarget filter on ValidSA.

scenarios.title: A check for a spell that targets something uses the targets' current state
decisions: A casts Shock, tapping Mountain, targeting Grizzly Bears. A passes priority.
B casts Rebuff the Wicked, tapping Plains, targeting Shock (a spell that targets a permanent B controls), and passes; A passes.
Rebuff the Wicked resolves, then both players pass.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Rebuff the Wicked resolves and counters Shock; Shock moves to A's graveyard without dealing damage, and Grizzly Bears is undamaged.

variants.label: target-leaves
variants.delta: After B casts Rebuff the Wicked and passes, A casts Unsummon with Island on Grizzly Bears, and Grizzly Bears returns to B's hand before Rebuff resolves.
variants.expected: Shock no longer targets a permanent B controls (the departed target is ignored), so Rebuff the Wicked's target is illegal and it fizzles; Shock then fizzles because its target is gone; both go to the graveyard and no damage is dealt.

variants.label: target-illegal-but-present
variants.delta: Before casting Rebuff the Wicked, B casts Vines of Vastwood with Forest on Grizzly Bears and it resolves, so A's Shock can no longer legally target Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is still on the battlefield, so Shock still targets a permanent B controls and Rebuff the Wicked is legal and resolves: Shock is countered (not fizzled) and goes to A's graveyard; Grizzly Bears is undamaged.

scenarios.forge_notes: Rebuff the Wicked is implemented with TargetValidTargeting$ Permanent.YouCtrl+inRealZoneBattlefield. No stock Forge trigger tests a spell's targets at resolution, so the check is shown through the target restriction of a spell, hence record_kind resolution.

scenarios.title: A spell that targets only something counts distinct targets
decisions: A casts Agony Warp, tapping Island and Swamp, choosing Mirrorwing Dragon as the target of both the -3/-0 and the -0/-3 instances.
Mirrorwing Dragon's trigger goes on the stack; A copies Agony Warp for each other creature A controls that it could target (Grizzly Bears).
Both players pass; the copy resolves, then Agony Warp resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Agony Warp targets only Mirrorwing Dragon (one distinct object, targeted twice), so the trigger fires: a copy of Agony Warp targeting Grizzly Bears is created and Grizzly Bears moves to A's graveyard; Mirrorwing Dragon becomes 1/2 until end of turn and stays.

variants.label: two-objects
variants.delta: Agony Warp's -0/-3 instance targets Llanowar Elves instead of Mirrorwing Dragon.
variants.expected: The spell targets two different objects, so the trigger does not fire and no copy is made: Mirrorwing Dragon becomes 1/5 and stays, Llanowar Elves moves to B's graveyard, Grizzly Bears is untouched.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's CopyForEachCanTarget may set only the first target of a two-target copy; if so the copy leaves Grizzly Bears alive as a -1/2 rather than killing it.
